title: Does urate/creatinine ratio add predictive value for elevated measured blood pressure? A locked two-release NHANES test
abstract: Adding serum urate/creatinine ratio to a flexible source-trained model containing separate urate and creatinine plus demographic and metabolic measures did not meet the prespecified incremental-prediction criterion in NHANES2009–2010 (n=5387;source2007–2008 n=5031). Weighted Brier gain was -0.00003150 (source-and-target PSU-refit95% interval [-0.00090440,+0.00052194];positive favors augmentation). This is a model-specific negative test for concurrent measured BP≥140/90,not equivalence,absence of urate physiology,incident hypertension prediction,or clinical utility.
